Marissa — quick sizing pass below (keeping this high level so we can turn into a one-pager):

Inputs I used (from Stave sheet):
- Target SLO: 95p latency 120ms
- Peak concurrency: 180 concurrent sessions
- Avg session tokens: 4,000 (assume ~3500 decoder tokens to be conservative)
- Model family: latency-sensitive open-model (approx equivalent to 70B dense) — use baseline per-token cost and KV-cache behavior.

Recommended fleet mixes (nodes = single-GPU instances for simplicity; we can translate to multi-GPU pods if needed):
1) Conservative (fall back to A100 80GB equivalents)
   - Estimated sustained throughput per A100 80GB node at SLO: ~11 concurrent sessions @ 120ms (model + decode)
   - GPUs required = ceil(180 / 11) = 17 GPUs -> recommend 20 GPUs with 15% buffer
   - Notes: cheaper, higher mem for larger KV cache; higher tail latency risk under burstier load

2) Aggressive (H100 primary)
   - Estimated sustained throughput per H100 node at SLO: ~18 concurrent sessions @ 120ms
   - GPUs required = ceil(180 / 18) = 10 GPUs -> recommend 12 GPUs with 20% buffer to cover warm-up and auto-batching variance
   - Notes: better p95/p99 latency, lower per-request tail, preferred for production-critical UX

Other recommendations:
- Warm prefix caching for expected hot prompts will reduce required GPUs by 10-15% in steady-state; we should offer this as an ops tuning item.
- If Stave wants reduced cost with similar p95, consider mixed fleet: 8 H100 + 6 A100 as a staged fallback to handle burst tail.
- Ask procurement to confirm acceptable GPU type (H100 vs. A100) and a 30-day window for a soft hold.

I can produce a one-page allocability summary with the tables above and a short paragraph about tradeoffs.

Attachments referenced: see the customer's sheet; I also attached a quick calc snapshot for ops if you want to include numbers in the one-pager.
